source.title: The Myeloma Drug Lenalidomide Promotes the Cereblon-Dependent Destruction of Ikaros Proteins

claims.statement: Lenalidomide promotes cereblon association with IKZF1 and IKZF3.
Cereblon-dependent ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation are part of the reported mechanism.
Responses differ among the studied myeloma cell lines.
claims.context: Studied myeloma cell lines, not individual patient predictions

architecture_decision.decision: Keep the generic binding demos separate; first build an evidence-linked qualitative mechanism map.
architecture_decision.reason: Single-site occupancy omits substrate recruitment and protein turnover. No quantitative degradation or patient-response model is established.
architecture_decision.next_candidate_observable: Relative IKZF1 or IKZF3 protein abundance in a specified in-vitro assay
architecture_decision.next_candidate_model: Research-only protein-turnover model, only after usable assay data and assumptions are reviewed

missing_evidence: Extract concentration and time observations with units, controls, replicates and assay context.
Review supplementary methods and retain a dated source snapshot with a content hash.
Distinguish binary binding affinity, cellular degradation potency and clinical response endpoints.
Assess baseline synthesis/turnover and whether an indirect turnover model is identifiable from the available measurements.
Record uncertainty, variability and model-fit/reproduction checks before selecting quantitative parameters.
Establish a justified exposure-to-cell mapping before any future connection to the educational PK model.
parameter_policy: Null means not extracted or accepted for this proposed model. It does not claim the parameter is absent from all literature. Invented demo values are never promoted.
scope: Initial research plan only. No numerical fitting, simulation, efficacy, toxicity or dosing calculation. No clinical endpoint linkage or patient applicability is established.
